motions.item_title: HRD-TOR-26-001, Reservist Leave Policy Information
motions.text: Whereas Under the ESA, 2000, an employee is currently entitled to unpaid Reservist Leave for Canadian Forces training or deployment, provided they have at least two (2) months of continuous employment and Whereas if the employee is taking Reservist Leave because they are deployed to a Canadian Forces operation inside Canada related to handling an emergency or its aftermath, there is no minimum employment requirement and Whereas recent amendments via the Working for Workers Act, 2023, have expanded this leave to also include recovery from deployment-related injuries or illnesses and Whereas the current ESA leave type creates a "break in service" in OMERS, which can potentially reduce an employee’s credited service and future retirement benefits and Whereas, currently, the Region has not elected to share the cost of contributions, meaning that the employee is responsible for both their portion and the employer's portion, known as "double contributions" and Whereas OMERS regulations permit the purchase of service for certain leaves of absence, including those mandated by statute, to restore full credited service. For Reservist Leave, the employee may elect to buy back the period by contributing their share of premiums, with the employer matching its portion. This process requires explicit employer approval and, for municipal entities, formal authorization via a bylaw to ensure compliance with the Municipal Act, 2001, and to allocate public funds appropriately and Whereas the proposed bylaw will honour the employee's service to both the municipality and the nation, while upholding OMERS eligibility rules and Whereas the there are minimal financial implications associated with approving the OMERS Reservist Leave By-law and where an employee elects to take a Reservist Leave for Canadian Forces training or deployment, the Region as the employer will make an equal OMERS contribution in accordance with subsection 12(3) of the Primary Plan, funded from within the existing divisional operating budget, Now therefore be it resolved that the Region of Waterloo adopt the OMERS Region of Waterloo Reservist Bylaw to authorize the Region to match OMERS contributions for employees purchasing OMERS broken service resulting from an approved Reservist Leave, in accordance with the Employment Standards Act (ESA), 2000.

motions.item_title: EES-WIM-26-012, Mannheim Service Area - Recommended Interim Risk Management Framework
motions.text: b) That the Region of Waterloo, at Council’s direction, allocate an additional 15 L/s from the Wilmot Centre Well Supply on an interim basis solely as a bridge measure until the side stream capacity solution is commissioned and operational, at which point the interim 15 L/s allocation shall automatically terminate and the water supply allocation shall revert to the previously approved levels. Further, that Regional staff provide a public report to Council confirming the termination of the interim 15 L/s allocation upon the side stream capacity solution becoming operational. Further, that any future consideration of additional water allocation from the Wilmot Supplies beyond the existing approved allocation levels be considered through the updated Water Supply Strategy and include: i) an assessment of impacts on surrounding private well properties; ii) costing and implementation options to connect impacted private well properties to the Integrated Servicing Utility (ISU) system; and iii) costing and implementation options for deep replacement wells or other measures that would provide a long-term, reliable and secure water supply for affected residents. Further, that as an interim measure, effective immediately and until such time as a new Well Interference Policy is adopted by Regional Council, the Region of Waterloo provide emergency water supply assistance to any Wilmot resident experiencing water loss or well interference, and that such assistance not be limited to properties located within the existing historic well interference compensation area. For greater certainty, the provision of emergency water supply assistance shall be considered a precautionary measure intended to protect residents’ access to water and shall not, in and of itself, be interpreted as an admission of responsibility, liability, or well interference by the Region of Waterloo. Further, that as an interim measure, effective immediately and until such time as a new Well Interference Policy is adopted by Regional Council, where a Wilmot resident reports water loss or well interference reasonably believed to be associated with Regional groundwater takings, the burden of demonstrating that Regional pumping is not the cause of the interference shall rest with the Region of Waterloo and not with the affected resident. Further, that these above interim measures be reviewed as part of the Well Interference Policy review currently being brought forward to Regional Council in August 2026, at which time Council may confirm, amend, or replace these requirements.

motions.item_title: Administration and Finance Committee - June 2, 2026
motions.text: The Administration and Finance Committee recommends as follows: 1. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the revised Municipal Election Compliance Audit Committee Terms of Reference, as set out in Appendix A attached to report PDL-LEG-26-011, dated June 2, 2026. 2. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2026 first quarter update as set out in report COR-CFN-26-009 dated June 2, 2026: a) Receive the 2026 First Quarter Update that shows implementation and financial progress towards delivery on the Region’s Annual Business Plan, in support of achieving the vision set out by Council in the Growing with Care 2023-2027 Strategic Plan; and b) Amend the 2026 Capital Budget as set out in Appendix B. 3. Whereas Under the ESA, 2000, an employee is currently entitled to unpaid Reservist Leave for Canadian Forces training or deployment, provided they have at least two (2) months of continuous employment and Whereas if the employee is taking Reservist Leave because they are deployed to a Canadian Forces operation inside Canada related to handling an emergency or its aftermath, there is no minimum employment requirement and Whereas recent amendments via the Working for Workers Act, 2023, have expanded this leave to also include recovery from deployment-related injuries or illnesses and Whereas the current ESA leave type creates a "break in service" in OMERS, which can potentially reduce an employee’s credited service and future retirement benefits and Whereas, currently, the Region has not elected to share the cost of contributions, meaning that the employee is responsible for both their portion and the employer's portion, known as "double contributions" and Whereas OMERS regulations permit the purchase of service for certain leaves of absence, including those mandated by statute, to restore full credited service. For Reservist Leave, the employee may elect to buy back the period by contributing their share of premiums, with the employer matching its portion. This process requires explicit employer approval and, for municipal entities, formal authorization via a bylaw to ensure compliance with the Municipal Act, 2001, and to allocate public funds appropriately and Whereas the proposed bylaw will honour the employee's service to both the municipality and the nation, while upholding OMERS eligibility rules and Whereas the there are minimal financial implications associated with approving the OMERS Reservist Leave By-law and where an employee elects to take a Reservist Leave for Canadian Forces training or deployment, the Region as the employer will make an equal OMERS contribution in accordance with subsection 12(3) of the Primary Plan, funded from within the existing divisional operating budget, Now therefore be it resolved that the Region of Waterloo adopt the OMERS Region of Waterloo Reservist Bylaw to authorize the Region to match OMERS contributions for employees purchasing OMERS broken service resulting from an approved Reservist Leave, in accordance with the Employment Standards Act (ESA), 2000. 4. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve a By-law to delegate authority to the outgoing council to pass by-law(s) to authorize the potential adoption of the prudent investor standard, as set out in report COR-TRY-26-016 dated June 2, 2026. 5. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2027 Plan and Budget as set out in report COR-CFN-008 dated June 2, 2026: a) That staff be provided direction to present 2027 Plan and Budget timetable schedule to the incoming Regional Chair as set out in Appendix A.

And that Appendix B to Report TSD-TRP-26-010, Street Design Guidelines, be amended by adding the following as a fifth principle in Chapter 1 under Guiding Principles: 5. Reflect the Region’s urban, rural, agricultural, and township contexts The Regional road network serves a diverse range of urban, suburban, settlement-area, rural, agricultural, employment, and natural contexts. Street design should respond to the primary function, surrounding land use, operating conditions, maintenance requirements, drainage needs, goods movement, agricultural operations, emergency access, and local community character of each corridor. While safety, accessibility, active transportation, transit-supportive design, and green infrastructure remain important objectives, the appropriate design solution will vary by context. Distinct parts of the Regional network, including rural roads, agricultural corridors, township main streets, industrial corridors, and commercial main streets, should be designed in keeping with their respective contexts and local needs while supporting the safe and efficient movement of people and goods, as well as appropriate access to adjacent businesses, services, and community destinations. And that staff be authorized to make any necessary page, formatting, numbering, or consequential wording updates to accommodate the addition of this principle.

motions.item_title: EES-WIM-26-013, Supporting Information for June 3, 2026 Council Resolutions
motions.text: Whereas through ongoing work and updates to the Water Supply Strategy, Regional staff have identified a water capacity constraint within the Mannheim Service Area, which supplies water to Kitchener, Waterloo, and parts of Cambridge, Woolwich, and Wilmot. As a result, the Region of Waterloo has been unable to enter into any new servicing agreements or support the approval of development applications within this service area, until such time that sufficient capacity becomes available; Whereas the Region continues to work closely with its municipal partners on moving short term, medium term and long-term solutions forward as expeditiously as possible; Whereas Regional Council approved a Water Capacity Allocation Policy on May 6, 2026, for the Mannheim Service Area, which determines how available water will be allocated once it becomes available; Whereas Regional Council approved the Interim Risk Management Framework on June 3, 2026, which assesses how staged development could proceed under certain risk-based conditions in the Mannheim Service Area; Whereas the approved Interim Risk Management Framework outlined estimated water allocations to be provided to Area Municipalities by the Region on a quarterly basis, and where it is anticipated that growth would be supported by the end of September 2026; Whereas on June 3, 2026, Regional Council approved an additional allocation of 15 L/s from Wilmot Centre on an interim basis; Therefore, Be It Resolved that on July 1, 2026, 20L/s be assigned to Area Municipalities in alignment with the Council approved allocation policy and the IRMF, to be available for use no earlier than September 30, 2026; And further, be it resolved that future water allocations be assigned to Area Municipalities, by the Region, prior to, or on, the first day of the applicable quarter, beginning on October 1, 2026 for water to be available for use not sooner than the last day of the applicable quarter.

motions.item_title: PDL-GDS-26-018, Forward Looking Service Agreements (Response to Resolution 4)
motions.text: Whereas through ongoing work and updates to the Water Supply Strategy, Region of Waterloo staff have identified a water capacity constraint within the Mannheim Service Area, which supplies water to Kitchener, Waterloo, and parts of Cambridge, Woolwich, and Wilmot. As a result, the Region has currently been unable to enter into any new servicing agreements or support the approval of development applications within this service area, until such time that sufficient capacity becomes available; Whereas the Region continues to work closely with its municipal partners on moving short, medium, and long-term solutions forward as expeditiously as possible; Whereas Regional Council approved a Water Capacity Allocation Policy on May 6, 2026, for the Mannheim Service Area, which determines how available water will be allocated once it becomes available: Whereas Regional Council approved the Interim Risk Management Framework on June 3, 2026, which assesses how staged development can proceed under certain risk-based conditions in the Mannheim Service Area; Whereas the details of any Municipal Forward Facing/Looking Servicing Agreements (MFSA’s) rest solely with Area Municipalities with respect to Planning Act and Building Code Act approvals; Whereas there are existing draft plans of subdivision that received draft approval prior to May 6, 2026, and which require a servicing agreement as a condition of draft plan approval, may be exempt from this motion; Therefore, be it resolved that the Region of Waterloo prepare an administrative agreement in conjunction with Area Municipalities by July 8, 2026 for execution by all relevant parties to implement the Regional Water Allocation Framework which will enable water allocation by the Region to an area municipalities in accordance with the Interim Risk Management Framework (IRMF) allocation schedule, as presented on June 3, 2026, with the following: Estimated Overall Allocation July 1, 2026 - 20 L/S October 1, 2026 - 40 L/S January 1, 2027 - 55 L/S July 1, 2028 - 25 L/S October 1, 2028 - 50 L/S July 1, 2030 - 45 L/S October 1, 2030 - 60 L/S and January 1, 2031 - 20 L/S; and, Further, Be It Resolved that such Administrative Agreements aim to include the following provisions, namely: Requirement for area municipalities to report all building permits to the Region for ongoing monitoring of water allocated against their share of the above allocation table, Notification processes for the Region to inform area municipalities if available water capacity is more than projected in the above table, or available earlier than expected, Notification timing provisions for the Region to notify Area Municipalities if it cannot meet the IRMF allocation schedule as listed above, Force Majeure clause, in case the Region is unable to meet its anticipated additional allocations due to an act outside of its control; and Further, Be It Resolved that the Region of Waterloo enable any area municipality to enter into Forward Facing/Looking Servicing Agreements for developments subject to the allocation table above; and Further, Be It Resolved that the Region coordinate any required regional approvals, required by an Area Municipality’s Forward Facing Servicing Agreements (MFSA), such approvals not to be withheld as long as the MFSA’s were issued within the parameters of the above allocation tables and the requirements of such approvals are met; And Finally, Be It Resolved that except in the case of draft plans of subdivision that were draft approved prior to May 6, and which may be exempt from this motion, all Forward Facing/Looking Servicing Agreements shall be executed between an Area Municipality and the property owner, in accordance with the overall water allocation granted to an Area Municipality by the Region.

motions.text: 1. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo waive the following provisions of By-Law 16-032, as amended (the “Purchasing By-Law): (i) the competitive procurement process and (ii) section 35, for water capacity supporting projects as identified in Appendix A of report COR-TRY-26-023, dated July 8, 2026, where required, to support commitments under the Council-approved Interim Risk Management Framework (IRMF), and delegate to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) such authorizations in accordance with the following: a. the Chief Administrative Office (CAO) may authorize the waiver of the competitive procurement process of the Purchasing By-Law, regardless of their value, for the water capacity projects identified in Appendix A, provided that: i. the CAO is satisfied that waiving the competitive procurement process is required in meeting the Region’s commitments to allocating water supply capacity under the IRMF; ii. compliance with the Purchasing By-Law cannot reasonably be followed to complete the project within the required timeframe; and iii. sufficient funding is included in the approved project budget or other water capacity projects identified in Appendix A; b. the Chief Administrative Office (CAO) may approve the disbursement of additional funds or reallocation of funds with respect to the purchase of goods or services that are already authorized in accordance with the Purchasing By-Law, regardless of their value, for the water capacity projects identified in Appendix A, provided that: iv. the CAO is satisfied the disbursement of additional funds or reallocation of funds is required in meeting the Region’s commitments to allocating water supply capacity under the IRMF; v. compliance with section 35 of the Purchasing By-Law cannot reasonably be followed to complete the project within the required timeframe; and vi. sufficient funding is included in the approved project budget or other water capacity projects identified in Appendix A. 2. Further, Regional Council directs that the following applies with respect to (1) above: prior to waiving the competitive procurement process, approving the disbursement of additional funds or the reallocation of funds under this authority, as the case may be, the CAO shall consult with the Chief Purchasing Officer (CPO) to confirm that the proposed change is within the scope of this authority and that the appropriate procurement process, contract amendment process, and documentation requirements are followed, as applicable; staff report monthly to Council on any waiving of the competitive procurement process, approving of the disbursement of additional funds or the reallocation of funds under this authority, and include information such as the project, vendor, selection process, description of the change, amount, funding source, the risk or urgency being addressed, and the rationale for use of the waiver; and the said waiver and delegated authority shall expire on December 31, 2028, after which any continuation would be subject to further Council review and approval. be in place only until June 30, 2027 and further, that the new Council be fully briefed on the water issue ahead of the 2027 budget, including staff delegation provisions so that they can consider if they want to proceed with them.

motions.item_title: Councillor D. McCabe
motions.text: Whereas the Region of Waterloo’s drinking water infrastructure is essential to the delivery of safe, reliable service to all residents, commercial and industrial businesses, institutions and other corporations across the community; and Whereas water conservation and water efficiency measures are needed in new buildings, including residential developments, and are important to managing long-term water demand, supporting sustainable growth, and reducing pressure on municipal water infrastructure; and Whereas the Maple Grove Water Treatment Plant and the Cambridge 2W Booster Pumping Station are important projects for the future of the Region’s water system, and timely actions are necessary to support long-term system reliability, operational resilience, and asset stewardship; and Whereas construction of the Maple Grove Water Treatment Plant and the Cambridge 2W Booster Pumping Station are scheduled to begin in 2028/2029; and Whereas the Environmental Assessment for this work is already complete for the Maple Grove Water Treatment Plant and underway for the Cambridge 2W Booster Pumping Station; and Whereas ensuring that the water capacity constraint is addressed and resolved as expediently as possible requires building the Maple Grove Water Treatment Plant and the Cambridge 2W Booster Pumping Station in a timely manner; and Therefore Be It Resolved That , while ensuring prudent oversight of financial, operational, and program impacts; Regional Council direct staff to review the 10-year capital plan for water and wastewater projects and report back to Council no later than the end of August 2026 on the feasibility of advancing the Maple Grove Booster Pumping Station design construction and the Cambridge 2W Booster Pumping Station design/construction so that work may commence in 2026/2027; and That the staff report include: a. an assessment of the readiness of each project to proceed in 2027, including design status, procurement requirements, regulatory approvals, operational constraints, and construction feasibility; b. the financial implications of accelerating these projects, including any impacts on the water and wastewater capital program, reserves, debt financing, rate-supported budgets, and the timing of other capital priorities; c. the risks, benefits, and service implications associated with advancing the projects to 2026/2027, as compared with maintaining the current schedule; and d. recommendations on implementation options, timelines, and any required amendments to the capital plan or budget for Council’s consideration. e. Provide a critical-path schedule identifying the earliest achievable dates for design completion, procurement, approvals, construction commencement, commissioning, and in-service capacity for each project, together with the specific Council decisions, budget amendments, staffing resources, procurement steps, regulatory approvals, and third-party dependencies required to achieve those dates; and f. estimates of the additional water capacity, expressed in litres per second and equivalent residential/employment growth capacity, expected from each project and from both projects combined, together with an updated Scenario 2 Water Forecast showing the effect of advancing the projects to 2026/2027 compared with the current 2028/2029 schedule.

motions.item_title: Councillor D. Craig
motions.text: Whereas municipal property taxes continue to represent a continual and growing expense for households, businesses, and and seniors living on fixed incomes, And whereas, inflation is only one measure of affordability and does not fully reflect residents’ financial circumstances or their ability to absorb additional tax increases, And whereas, the true ability to pay is influenced by household income growth, housing costs, utility costs, food prices, transportation expenses and others cost of living pressures, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT: Regional Council direct staff to develop and implement a “Household Affordability Framework” to be included annually as part of the Region’s budgeting process, And that, the framework include where practical : Medium household income trends within the Region of Waterloo; Property tax burden as a percentage of household incomes; Cost of living indicators including housing, utilities, food, transportation, and insurance costs; Affordably impacts on seniors and residents living on fixed incomes; Comparison of proposed budget increases against inflation, population growth, and assessment growth; Historical trends in municipal tax increases and cumulative impacts on households; AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED; That staff report annually on the affordability implications of the proposed budget and identify the impact of tax supported budget increases on the average household, And that the Household Affordability Framework be used as an advisory tool to support Council budget deliberations and long term financial planning.

motions.item_title: Councillor C. James Motion re: Information Report on Transit Connectivity Gaps and Service Enhancement Opportunities
motions.text: WHEREAS the Region of Waterloo's 2023–2027 Strategic Plan, Growing with Care, supports equitable access to services, climate-aligned growth, and innovative approaches to service delivery; AND WHEREAS access to reliable public transit is essential for connecting residents to employment, education, health care, housing, and community services; AND WHEREAS some growing and underserved areas of Waterloo Region experience transit connectivity challenges, including first-mile and last-mile barriers, service coverage gaps, and limited access to conventional transit; AND WHEREAS Grand River Transit’s Business Plan identifies the need to expand service, improve connections, support growth, and enhance access to transit across Waterloo Region; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. Regional Council direct staff to identify transit connectivity gaps in growing urban centres and underserved areas of Waterloo Region, including new neighbourhoods, which could be addressed in the short term; 2. That staff evaluate potential options to address these gaps, and assess how such options align with and support the objectives of the Grand River Transit Business Plan; 3. That staff assess the feasibility, anticipated capital and operating costs, implementation requirements, ridership potential, and service impacts associated with any proposed options; 4. That staff identify potential funding opportunities, including provincial and federal programs, grants, partnerships, fare changes and other external funding sources that may support these options; and That staff report back to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee ahead of the 2027 Budget with findings, cost estimates, funding opportunities, and recommendations for Council's consideration.

motions.item_title: Councillor C. James Motion Re: Information Report on Data Centres: Best Practices and Community Safeguards
motions.text: MAIN MOTION AS AMENDED WHEREAS data centres are an important and growing part of the digital economy and are being developed in communities across Ontario and Canada; AND WHEREAS data centres vary significantly in size, function, and resource requirements, including electricity, water, telecommunications infrastructure, and land; AND WHEREAS recent data centre growth is being driven in part by artificial intelligence, which can require significant electricity and water for cooling; AND WHEREAS the Region of Waterloo is growing and faces increasing demand on drinking water, wastewater, electricity, and other critical infrastructure; AND WHEREAS the Region relies primarily on groundwater for drinking water, making water-intensive development a matter of regional interest; AND WHEREAS Council should understand how data centre development may affect infrastructure capacity, environmental sustainability, and economic development; AND WHEREAS municipalities are beginning to assess the opportunities, risks, and policy issues related to data centres; AND WHEREAS Council would benefit from objective information before considering any future policy direction; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Regional staff prepare an information report on data centre development and its potential implications for the Region of Waterloo, including: 1. Economic opportunities, including investment, innovation, construction jobs, temporary and permanent jobs, and support for the digital economy. 2. Infrastructure needs and impacts, including: cumulative electricity demand relative to available grid capacity; water consumption based on different cooling technologies; wastewater servicing; telecommunications infrastructure; emergency services planning. 3. Environmental considerations and best practices, including water use, electricity demand, greenhouse gas emissions, energy efficiency, water conservation, sustainable cooling, and responsible operations, and potential impacts on groundwater, source water, stormwater, wastewater, air quality, noise, spills and hazardous materials, including cumulative impacts and applicable provincial environmental approvals and monitoring requirements. 4. Fiscal considerations, including servicing needs, capital and operating costs, assessment impacts, and how upgrade costs are allocated among operators, utilities, are municipalities, and existing ratepayers. 5. Transparency and accountability, including best practices for public reporting on energy use, water use, cooling systems, and impact on environment. 6. A jurisdictional scan to identify best practices for balancing economic development, environmental protection, infrastructure capacity, and community interests. 7. Potential advocacy to the Province of Ontario for a consistent regulatory framework for data centre development that: protects drinking water resources, groundwater, and the environment; plans and manages electricity, water, wastewater, and other infrastructure impacts; sets clear environmental, resource stewardship, and transparency requirements; ensures municipalities and existing ratepayers do not face undue costs for servicing data centres; supports responsible economic development and investment; gives municipalities clear tools to assess and manage proposed developments. Indigenous perspectives, including potential impacts on traditional lands, water, the environment and culturally significant areas, and opportunities for appropriate engagement with local First Nations and Indigenous communities. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff report back to Council by Q1 2027.

motions.text: WHEREAS the Mayor of a municipality has a responsibility to advocate for the interests of that municipality, while the Regional Chair must provide fair and impartial leadership for the Region as a whole; AND WHEREAS allowing one individual to serve simultaneously as Mayor and Regional Chair creates the potential for real or perceived conflicts of interest when municipal and regional priorities differ; AND WHEREAS combining Strong Mayor and Strong Chair powers in one individual would significantly concentrate authority and could diminish the role of locally elected councillors and collective council decision-making; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT: Regional Council oppose any governance model allowing one person to serve simultaneously as Mayor and Regional Chair; Regional Council express concern about the concentration of Strong Mayor and Strong Chair powers in one individual; This resolution be forwarded to the Premier of Ontario, the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing, local MPPs, area municipalities and affected regional municipalities.

motions.item_title: Councillor P. Wolf Motion re: Housing and Homelessness
motions.text: Whereas the Region of Waterloo is responsible for funding and coordinating homelessness services, including emergency shelters, supportive and transitional housing, and outreach programming; and Whereas Council has a responsibility to ensure that new investments in housing and homelessness services do not unintentionally reinforce geographic inequities but instead contribute to a more balanced and accessible regional system; and Whereas the Region's commitment to addressing homelessness must include, not only increasing overall capacity, but also ensuring equitable access to services across all municipalities, including a more equitable distribution of funding and services dedicated specifically to women; and Whereas there are only 20 emergency homeless shelter beds for women in Cambridge, 42 total throughout the entire Region and only 80 of all shelter beds dedicated to men are in Cambridge while the remaining 130 are in Kitchener-Waterloo; 120 all gender beds in Kitchener-Waterloo and Whereas the single women’s shelter in Cambridge has been forced to deny almost 300 requests for services due to consistently being at capacity since August 2025; and Whereas residents experiencing homelessness in Cambridge are frequently required to travel outside their community to access shelter and other homelessness supports services, creating additional barriers to safety, continuity of care, and connection to local supports; and Whereas Porchlight Counselling and Addiction Services’ winter warming centre for men operated at a minimum of 128% and maximum of 198% throughout its 2025-6 seasonal operations and their request to operate this centre 365 days a year was rejected by the Region, the reason given being a lack of funding; and Whereas Thrive HIV Prevention and Support, which operates the Multi Agency Community Space out of 150 Main in Cambridge - the single drop-in space for individuals experiencing homelessness in Cambridge - is only funded to operate during afternoons, despite an immense need for extended operating hours; and Whereas YWCA Cambridge has requested that the Region fund a 365-day, low-barrier overnight drop-in for women in Cambridge and been repeatedly told there is not adequate funding to do so, despite the lack of any overnight spaces for women in Cambridge existing outside of the 20-bed shelter; and Whereas the Region recently granted Kitchener a 365-day, 22.5-hr-a-day shelter; and Whereas such recent funding decisions only further concentrate services in one city and predominantly on programs dedicated to men or which are co-ed, while neglecting to address the immense lack of services in Cambridge; and Whereas research consistently shows that women avoid co-ed spaces out of fear for their safety, effectively rendering co-ed spaces for men only, further exacerbating the discrepancy in service availability for men versus women; Therefore, Be It Resolved That Regional Council direct staff to bring a report to the November 2026 Community & Health Services Committee with recommendations related to: the principle that major investments in homelessness and infrastructure be accompanied by a strategy to improve service access and capacity in underserved municipalities; and future homelessness-related capital funding allocations exceeding 1 million include an assessment of geographic distribution impacts and a requirement to identify complementary investments in underserved municipalities where gaps exist; and improving homelessness service capacity and access in underserved municipalities, including Cambridge, as part of future homelessness system planning and capital budget deliberations; and the application of Gender-Based Analysis Plus lens to all investments in homelessness and infrastructure to ensure a gender equitable distribution in funding and services across the Region of Waterloo.

motions.item_title: Councillor D. Craig Motion Re: River Crossings in Cambridge
motions.text: WHEREAS the Grand and Speed Rivers create significant natural barriers within Cambridge and concentrate vehicular, pedestrian and cycling movements on a limited number of crossings; AND WHEREAS continued population and employment growth will place additional demands on Cambridge's transportation network and existing river crossings; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT as part of the Region of Waterloo's current review of the Regional road and transportation system, staff be directed to: Assess whether existing Grand and Speed River crossings in Cambridge will provide sufficient capacity and network resiliency to accommodate projected growth to 2051; Assess the need and opportunities for additional vehicular, pedestrian and cycling crossings, including their potential to improve traffic movement, emergency and alternate-route access, active transportation connectivity and overall network resiliency; Review previous studies and assumptions concerning additional river crossings to determine whether they remain appropriate in light of current growth projections, development patterns and transportation demands; Identify any potential future crossing corridors that should be protected through long-term transportation and land-use planning; and Report back to Regional Council with findings and recommendations for consideration in the Region's long term transportation plans.

motions.item_title: CHS Summary - September 8, 2026
motions.text: The Community and Health Services Committee recommends as follows: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the Response Time Performance Plan (RTPP) for 2027, outlined below, in accordance with the Ambulance Act, O. Reg. 257/00, under Part VIII, Response Time Standards, as amended by O. Reg. 251/25, s. 5, as outlined in PHP-PSV-26-005, dated September 8, 2026. Sudden Cardiac Arrest (SCA) – 6 minutes or less 70% of the time. (Note: Ministry of Health target is 50%.) CTAS 1 – 8 minutes or less 70% of the time. CTAS 2 – 10 minutes or less 80% of the time. CTAS 3 – 15 minutes or less 80% of the time. CTAS 4 – 20 minutes or less 80% of the time. CTAS 5 – 25 minutes or less 80% of the time. Whereas the Region of Waterloo is responsible for funding and coordinating homelessness services, including emergency shelters, supportive and transitional housing, and outreach programming; and Whereas Council has a responsibility to ensure that new investments in housing and homelessness services do not unintentionally reinforce geographic inequities but instead contribute to a more balanced and accessible regional system; and Whereas the Region's commitment to addressing homelessness must include, not only increasing overall capacity, but also ensuring equitable access to services across all municipalities, including a more equitable distribution of funding and services dedicated specifically to women; and Whereas there are only 20 emergency homeless shelter beds for women in Cambridge, 42 total throughout the entire Region and only 80 of all shelter beds dedicated to men are in Cambridge while the remaining 130 are in Kitchener-Waterloo; 120 all gender beds in Kitchener-Waterloo and Whereas the single women’s shelter in Cambridge has been forced to deny almost 300 requests for services due to consistently being at capacity since August 2025; and Whereas residents experiencing homelessness in Cambridge are frequently required to travel outside their community to access shelter and other homelessness supports services, creating additional barriers to safety, continuity of care, and connection to local supports; and Whereas Porchlight Counselling and Addiction Services’ winter warming centre for men operated at a minimum of 128% and maximum of 198% throughout its 2025-6 seasonal operations and their request to operate this centre 365 days a year was rejected by the Region, the reason given being a lack of funding; and Whereas Thrive HIV Prevention and Support, which operates the Multi Agency Community Space out of 150 Main in Cambridge - the single drop-in space for individuals experiencing homelessness in Cambridge - is only funded to operate during afternoons, despite an immense need for extended operating hours; and Whereas YWCA Cambridge has requested that the Region fund a 365-day, low-barrier overnight drop-in for women in Cambridge and been repeatedly told there is not adequate funding to do so, despite the lack of any overnight spaces for women in Cambridge existing outside of the 20-bed shelter; and Whereas the Region recently granted Kitchener a 365-day, 22.5-hr-a-day shelter; and Whereas such recent funding decisions only further concentrate services in one city and predominantly on programs dedicated to men or which are co-ed, while neglecting to address the immense lack of services in Cambridge; and Whereas research consistently shows that women avoid co-ed spaces out of fear for their safety, effectively rendering co-ed spaces for men only, further exacerbating the discrepancy in service availability for men versus women; Therefore, Be It Resolved That Regional Council direct staff to bring a report to the November 2026 Community & Health Services Committee with recommendations related to: the principle that major investments in homelessness and infrastructure be accompanied by a strategy to improve service access and capacity in underserved municipalities; and future homelessness-related capital funding allocations exceeding 1 million include an assessment of geographic distribution impacts and a requirement to identify complementary investments in underserved municipalities where gaps exist; and improving homelessness service capacity and access in underserved municipalities, including Cambridge, as part of future homelessness system planning and capital budget deliberations; and the application of Gender-Based Analysis Plus lens to all investments in homelessness and infrastructure to ensure a gender equitable distribution in funding and services across the Region of Waterloo.

motions.item_title: Councillor P. Wolf Motion re: Drivers of Tourism Funding Allocation Criteria
motions.text: WHEREAS the Region of Waterloo's Cultural Drivers of Tourism program provides funding from the Municipal Accommodation Tax (MAT) Reserve to support arts, cultural, and heritage organizations that attract visitors to Waterloo Region; and WHEREAS hotels located throughout Waterloo Region generate the Municipal Accommodation Tax revenues that fund this program; and WHEREAS the 2026 funding allocations resulted in Cambridge-based organizations receiving approximately $3,000 of the $250,000 available through the program, despite Cambridge being home to a significant number of accommodation providers contributing to the MAT Reserve; WHEREAS a sustainable cultural tourism strategy should recognize both visitor attraction outcomes and the contribution of municipalities that generate the revenues supporting the program; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Regional Council direct staff to review the Cultural Drivers of Tourism funding formula and eligibility criteria to determine whether amendments are warranted to ensure a more equitable geographic distribution of funding across the Region's municipalities; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the review include consideration of: 1. The relationship between Municipal Accommodation Tax revenue generation and funding allocations; 2. Mechanisms to ensure all municipalities receive fair consideration under the program; 3. The long-term impact of current allocation practices on cultural development and tourism growth in municipalities receiving minimal funding; and 4. Alternative funding models that balance visitor attraction metrics with regional equity objectives. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff report back to Council with recommendations prior to the next Cultural Drivers of Tourism funding intake.

motions.item_title: Councillor C. James Motion re: Stanley Park Community Association Mural Project
motions.text: WHEREAS the late Kari Williams served the residents of Waterloo Region with dedication, compassion, and a strong commitment to community well-being; and WHEREAS Kari Williams was a passionate supporter of the Stanley Park Eats program, which provides meals and support to community members in need; and WHEREAS the Stanley Park Community Association is leading a community mural project on the Stanley Park Eats serving hut; and WHEREAS the mural has been inspired by Kari Williams' commitment to addressing food insecurity and supporting the Stanley Park community; and WHEREAS the project has received funding through a $6,500 LoveMyHood grant from the City of Kitchener and contributions from the Stanley Park Community Association, and community fundraising efforts; and WHEREAS community art projects help create vibrant public spaces and strengthen neighbourhood pride; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Regional Council approve a one-time grant of $2,000 from the Municipal Accommodation Tax Reserve Public Art Reserve Fund to the Stanley Park Community Association to support the Stanley Park Eats mural project; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that Regional Council recognizes the lasting contributions of Kari Williams to the Stanley Park community and Waterloo Region; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Commissioner of Corporate Services be authorized to take all necessary administrative actions to implement this resolution.

motions.text: The Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee recommends as follows: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the expropriation of lands for improvements to University Avenue East (between Weber Street North and Albert Street), in the City of Waterloo, in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, as detailed in Report CAO-LEG-26-002, dated October 6, 2026, described as follows: Fee Simple Partial Taking: Part of Lot 19, Plan 494, being Part 1 on 58R-22340, City of Waterloo, Part of PIN 22368-0246 (244-248 King Street North, City of Waterloo) Part of Lots 18 and 19, Plan 494, being Part 4 on 58R-22340, City of Waterloo, Part of PIN 22368-0098 (15 University Avenue East, City of Waterloo) Part of Lot 70, Municipal Compiled Plan of the Subdivision of Lot 13, German Company Tract, being Part 11 on 58R-22340, City of Waterloo Part of PIN 22360-0014 (64 University Avenue East, City of Waterloo) Part of Lot 70, Municipal Compiled Plan of the Subdivision of Lot 13, German Company Tract, being Part 12 on 58R-22340, City of Waterloo, Part of PIN 22360-0059 (66-68 University Avenue East, City of Waterloo) Permanent Easement – Hydro Aerial and Anchoring: The right and easement, being an easement in gross, for itself, its successors and assigns and anyone authorized by it, in perpetuity to, at any time enter upon the following properties for purposes of relocated aerial hydro utility and associated anchoring. All related infrastructure, and all appurtenances thereto, which may be determined necessary from time to time, and for all such purposes together with the free, unimpeded and unobstructed access for itself, its successors and assigns, servants, agents, contractors, workers and anyone authorized by it, and vehicles, supplies and equipment at all times and for all purposes and things necessary for or incidental to the exercise and enjoyment of the right and easement: Part of Lot 19, Plan 494, being Parts 2 and 3 on 58R-22340, City of Waterloo, Part of PIN 22368-0246 (244-248 King Street North, City of Waterloo) Part of Lot 19, Plan 494, being Part 5 on 58R-22340, City of Waterloo, Part of PIN 22368-0098 (15 University Avenue East, City of Waterloo And that staff be instructed to register a Plan of Expropriation for the properties within three months of the granting of the approval to expropriate the properties, as required by the Expropriations Act; And that the registered owners be served with a Notice of Expropriation, Notice of Election and a Notice of Possession for the properties after the registration of the Plan of Expropriation and the Regional Solicitor is authorized to take any and all actions required to enforce such Notices including but not limited to any application pursuant to Section 40 of the Expropriations Act; And that the Regional Solicitor is authorized to enter into an agreement with the registered owners, or to make an application under Section 39 of the Expropriations Act, to adjust the date for possession specified in the Notice of Possession as may be required; And that all above-referenced fee simple partial takings situated adjacent to an existing Regional public highway be acquired for road widening purposes and therefore be deemed to form part of the adjacent public highway in accordance with subsection 31(6) of the Municipal Act, 2001; And that if no agreement as to compensation is made with an owner, the statutory Offer of Compensation and payment be served upon the registered owners of the properties in the amount of the market value of the interests in the land as estimated by the Region’s appraiser in accordance with the Expropriations Act; And that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to execute any Indemnity agreement or other document related to payment of the statutory Offer of Compensation; And further that the Regional Solicitor be authorized to discontinue expropriation proceedings or any part thereof, in respect of the above described lands, or any part thereof, upon the registration on title of the required documentation to complete the transaction or if determined by the Commissioner, Engineering & Environmental Services, that such lands, or any part or interest thereof, are not required for the subject Project. WHEREAS the Region of Waterloo currently uses established methodologies to assess traffic noise along Regional roads; AND WHEREAS traffic-noise modelling and assessment practices continue to evolve; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT as part of Transportation Services’ 2027 work plan, staff review alternative and emerging methodologies used to calculate and assess traffic noise, including approaches used by other municipalities and transportation authorities; AND FURTHER THAT staff report back to Regional Council with their findings, including whether any changes to the Region’s current noise assessment methodology should be considered.

motions.item_title: Administration and Finance Committee Summary - October 6, 2026
motions.text: The Administration and Finance Committee recommends as follows: THAT the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, on behalf of the Waterloo Region Education and Public Network (WREPNET) partners, renew its agreement with Rogers Communications Canada Inc. for the provisioning and supply of a dark fibre network within the Region for a five (5) year period beginning September 1, 2026, subject to final CPI reconciliation and the material terms summarized in this report, with such agreement to be satisfactory to the Commissioner of Corporate Services and Regional Solicitor, as outlined in Report COR-ITS-26-001 dated October 6, 2026. THAT the Regional Municipality of Waterloo directs staff to review and update the Region’s Reserve and Reserve Fund Policy for consideration by the Administration & Finance Committee in Q2 2027, as outlined in report COR-CFN-26-021 dated October 6, 2026. WHEREAS the Region of Waterloo's Cultural Drivers of Tourism program provides funding from the Municipal Accommodation Tax (MAT) Reserve to support arts, cultural, and heritage organizations that attract visitors to Waterloo Region; and WHEREAS hotels located throughout Waterloo Region generate the Municipal Accommodation Tax revenues that fund this program; and WHEREAS the 2026 funding allocations resulted in Cambridge-based organizations receiving approximately $3,000 of the $250,000 available through the program, despite Cambridge being home to a significant number of accommodation providers contributing to the MAT Reserve; WHEREAS a sustainable cultural tourism strategy should recognize both visitor attraction outcomes and the contribution of municipalities that generate the revenues supporting the program; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Regional Council direct staff to review the Cultural Drivers of Tourism funding formula and eligibility criteria to determine whether amendments are warranted to ensure a more equitable geographic distribution of funding across the Region's municipalities; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the review include consideration of: The relationship between Municipal Accommodation Tax revenue generation and funding allocations; Mechanisms to ensure all municipalities receive fair consideration under the program; The long-term impact of current allocation practices on cultural development and tourism growth in municipalities receiving minimal funding; and Alternative funding models that balance visitor attraction metrics with regional equity objectives. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff report back to Council with recommendations prior to the next Cultural Drivers of Tourism funding intake. WHEREAS the late Kari Williams served the residents of Waterloo Region with dedication, compassion, and a strong commitment to community well-being; and WHEREAS Kari Williams was a passionate supporter of the Stanley Park Eats program, which provides meals and support to community members in need; and WHEREAS the Stanley Park Community Association is leading a community mural project on the Stanley Park Eats serving hut; and WHEREAS the mural has been inspired by Kari Williams' commitment to addressing food insecurity and supporting the Stanley Park community; and WHEREAS the project has received funding through the City of Kitchener and contributions from the Stanley Park Community Association, and community fundraising efforts; and WHEREAS community art projects help create vibrant public spaces and strengthen neighbourhood pride; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Regional Council approve a one-time grant of $2,000 from the Public Art Reserve Fund to the Stanley Park Community Association to support the Stanley Park Eats mural project; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that Regional Council recognizes the lasting contributions of Kari Williams to the Stanley Park community and Waterloo Region; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Commissioner of Corporate Services be authorized to take all necessary administrative actions to implement this resolution.
